name: From LLM to Agentic AI: How AI Systems Are Becoming Autonomous
snippet: From LLM to Agentic AI: How AI Systems Are Becoming Autonomous T18:17: A classic LLM interaction is stateless and single-pass: a prompt goes in, a completion comes out. The model cannot affect the world — it can only produce text. That’s a powerful tool, but a very limited agent. Agentic AI flips this equation. The LLM now operates as a control unit connected to the external world: it observes the environment, forms a plan, executes tools, and feeds its own output back as its next input. The core difference: Stateless completion → Stateful, multi-step task execution. A regular LLM gives you a recipe. An agent orders the groceries, updates your calendar, and pays the bill. Feature Classic LLM Agentic AI Memory Limited to context window Persistent, external storage World effect None (text only) API, DB, browser, shell… Control flow Single pass Cyclic, conditional Error recovery None Observe → retry Planning Implicit (CoT) Explicit, dynamic At the core of virtually every agentic system lies the ReAct loop (Reasoning + Acting). On each iteration, the model does three things: evaluates the current state, selects an action, and observes the result. Frameworks like LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI abstract this loop. But understanding the underlying mechanism is the key to moving beyond framework dependency. # If no tool call → model is done if response.stop_reason == "end_turn": return response.content[0].text Tool use is what transforms a text generator into an agent. The model doesn’t just describe what it would do — it does it by emitting a structured call that your runtime intercepts and executes. # Tool schema — what the model sees Memory is what separates from a stateless chatbot. There are four distinct memory types, each solving a different problem: Memory session Token buffer Conversation Episodic Past sessions DB “Last time you asked about X…” Vector/graph Company docs, domain facts Procedural Behavior patterns Prompt / fine-tune Tool usage preferences The context window is finite.
